'''Judy Leavitt Walker''' is an American mathematician. She is the Aaron Douglas Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]], where she chaired the mathematics department from 2012 through 2016 and currently serves as the Associate Vice Chancellor for Faculty Affairs. Her research is in the area of [[algebraic coding theory]].<ref name="cv">[http://www.math.unl.edu/~jwalker7/papers/vita.pdf Curriculum vitae], retrieved 2014-12-25.</ref>

In 2012, Walker became one of the inaugural [[Fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2014-12-25.</ref>

Throughout her career, Walker has worked on issues related to women in mathematics.  She is co-founder of the University of Nebraska's All Girls/All Math program for high school girls; she represented her department at the White House when they were recognized with a 1998 Presidential Award for Excellence in Science, Mathematics, and Engineering mentoring; and she is co-founder of the Nebraska Conference for Undergraduate Women in Mathematics.

==Education==
Walker graduated from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1990,<ref name="cv"/> and went on to graduate studies at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]], earning her Ph.D. in 1996 under the supervision of [[Nigel Boston]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Judy Leavitt Walker|id=4030}}</ref>

==Career==
She joined the University of Nebraska–Lincoln faculty in 1996, was promoted to full professor in 2006 and took up the Aaron Douglas Professorship in 2012.<ref name="cv"/> She held a visiting professorship at [https://www.epfl.ch École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne] (EPFL) during fall 2011.

==Academic interests==
Walker's research is in [[coding theory]], i.e., the study of error-correcting codes.  Her primary contributions have been in algebraic geometry codes and [[Low-density parity-check code|low-density parity check codes]].

* Outstanding Teaching and Instructional Creativity Award (University of Nebraska system, 2014)
* George Pólya Lecturer (Mathematical Association of America, 2009-2011)
* [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]] ([[Mathematical Association of America]], 2006)<ref name=web>{{Cite web|url=https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|title=Recipients of the Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics; Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|access-date=2024-10-07|archive-date=2024-06-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608175318/https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref>
* Irving Reiner Memorial Award (University of Illinois Department of Mathematics, 1996)
* Fellow of the [https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/ Association for Women in Mathematics] (2019)<ref>{{citation|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/|title=2019 Class of AWM Fellows|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|accessdate=2019-01-26}}</ref>
* 2021 class of Fellows of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.aaas.org/page/2021-fellows|title=2021 Fellows|publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science|access-date=2022-01-28}}</ref>
